title: Customer story / case study page template layout + reusable components (Docs site)
creator: Camila Reyes
description:
## Context
We’re launching a case study + customer reference program and need a reusable, developer-first customer story page template that can be used across the Docs site (and optionally mirrored on marketing surfaces later). The template must support:
- Quote callouts (short, scannable)
- An architecture diagram block (with caption + light/dark support)
- Metrics/results section with standardized disclaimer language (metrics may be ranges / methodology caveats)

This ticket focuses on page layout and reusable components (blocks) so Marketing/DevEx can publish stories quickly without bespoke design each time.

## Goals
1) Make customer stories easy to skim (developer-first, concrete proof, minimal fluff).
2) Ensure consistent placement and styling for: problem → solution → implementation → results → proof/disclaimers.
3) Provide drop-in components compatible with Docs theming and accessible by default.
4) Create a structure that works for both “public case study” pages and “lightweight story” pages where the customer won’t share exact metrics.

## Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Copywriting for a specific customer story (handled in separate workstreams).
- Implementing the components in code (tracked in ENG tickets/PRs).
- Designing the case studies landing page IA (ENG-9401 + docs PRs).

## Proposed page structure (v1)
1) Hero
- Customer name + optional logo
- One-line outcome statement (e.g., “Dedicated capacity with predictable p95 latency at scale”)
- Deployment mode badges (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Primary CTA: “Talk to sales” or “Request a demo” (optional for Docs)

2) At-a-glance summary (2-column)
- Use case (e.g., “Ecommerce search + chat assistant”)
- Team / personas (optional)
- Models / workload type (optional, careful with naming if restricted)
- Environment (Dedicated / VPC / on-prem)

3) Challenge / constraints
- Bullet-friendly; include constraints like compliance, latency SLOs, cost targets, regional requirements.

4) Solution (Redwood components used)
- Reference relevant product surfaces (Console, Optimize, routing policies, caching/batching, audit logs/KMS).

5) Implementation
- “What they built” and “How they deployed”
- Include Architecture diagram block

6) Results
- Metric cards (up to 3–5), supporting exact values OR ranges (e.g., “p95 latency: 220–280ms”)
- Include methodology notes as inline footnotes where needed

7) Quote callouts
- Pull quotes placed between sections (ideally after Solution and/or Results)
- Support attribution rules (Name, Title, Company) and “Anonymous customer” pattern

8) Proof / disclaimer block (required)
- Standardized “Metrics and methodology” disclaimer area with consistent styling.
- Must support:
  - “Reported by customer” vs “Measured by Redwood” toggles (copy-only for v1)
  - Ranges instead of exact values
  - Redaction statement (e.g., “Details adjusted to protect confidentiality.”)

9) CTA + related resources
- “See docs” / “Talk to us” / “Read more customer stories”
- Optional: link to eval harness, benchmark post, or product docs

## Components to design (reusable blocks)
- CustomerStoryHero
- BadgeRow (deployment mode, industry tags)
- SummaryGrid
- QuoteCallout (short + long variants)
- MetricCard (exact value) + MetricCardRange (range) + MetricFootnote style
- ArchitectureDiagramBlock (image, caption, alt text guidance, ‘Open image’ affordance)
- DisclaimerBlock (standardized, with info icon)
- CTASection (secondary, consistent across stories)

## Content + legal constraints
- Support “logo hidden” and “attribution hidden” variants.
- Metrics may be:
  - exact values,
  - ranges,
  - directional improvements only (e.g., “reduced p95 latency” without numbers).
- Must include a dedicated area where Legal-approved disclaimers can be placed without reworking layout.

## Accessibility requirements
- Quote callouts must maintain contrast and not rely on color alone.
- Metric cards must be readable with large text scaling.
- Architecture diagram must have:
  - required alt text field guidance,
  - optional long description pattern (link or expandable text) for complex diagrams.

## Deliverables
- Figma frame(s) for:
  - Full page template (desktop + mobile)
  - Component specs / variants (logo on/off, attribution on/off, metrics exact/range)
  - Example content filled in (use Northwind outline placeholders; no customer-confidential copy)
- Hand-off notes for DevEx/Engineering (spacing, typography tokens, responsive behavior)

## Acceptance criteria
- Page template works with:
  - at least 1 quote callout,
  - 1 architecture diagram,
  - 3 metric cards + disclaimer block.
- Has documented variants for anonymized stories (no logo, anonymous quote attribution).
- Clear guidance for where the metrics disclaimer goes and how it behaves on mobile.
- Components are consistent with Docs typography and spacing; no one-off colors.
- Accessibility checklist passed (contrast, semantic hierarchy guidance, alt text pattern).

## Links / references
- Docs implementation context: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-4821-add-case-studies-landing-page-and-template.json
- Navigation ticket: ENG-9401
- Program owner: Camila Reyes
- Messaging/narrative: Soojin Lee
- Technical validation/diagrams: Markus Klein / Simran Kaur

## Notes
If we can’t support fully interactive disclosure patterns in v1, we should still design the disclaimer block to be future-proof (space + structure) and keep v1 copy-only.
comments: 2025-10-03 (Soojin Lee): Strong preference for developer-first scanning: avoid large hero blocks; keep headline + proof above the fold. Also please include a pattern for when we’re only allowed to publish metric ranges or directional improvements.

2025-10-06 (Markus Klein): For the architecture diagram block, we should assume diagrams come from Solutions Eng exports (SVG/PNG). We need a consistent max width and a way to open in a new tab for readability. Also please include a short caption field (1–2 lines) for quick context.

2025-10-08 (Michael Grant): Disclaimers need to be visually separated from marketing copy. Recommend an always-present “Metrics and methodology” section to reduce the risk of a story being published without the required caveats. Also need an anonymization sentence pattern when customer requests it.

2025-10-10 (Tyler Benson): Operationally, Marketing will reuse these blocks across multiple pages. Any component variants should map to simple markdown/MDX frontmatter toggles (logo_on/off, attribution_on/off, metrics_mode=exact|range|directional). Even if engineering does the mapping later, naming the variants now will help.

2025-10-14 (Camila Reyes): Please include an example of a ‘reference-call ready’ quote callout: something that highlights reliability/fallbacks and doesn’t mention confidential infrastructure details. We’ve had customers want quote edits even after approval—keeping callouts short helps.

2025-10-18 (Update): Design delivered in Figma with desktop/mobile layouts + component variants. Added explicit anonymized attribution pattern and standardized disclaimer block placement directly under Results.
2025-10-21 (Closeout): Hand-off notes shared with DevEx and linked in docs PR review. Engineering confirmed the layout can be implemented with existing Docs tokens + a small set of new components.
